paragraphs: Air-gapped military datacenters serving multi-theater command queries must handle massive concurrent intelligence document summarization, satellite report classification, and automated battle damage assessment. Unpredictable sequence lengths lead to severe GPU memory waste under conventional contiguous tensor allocation, while PagedAttention page table thrashing can cause sudden inference latency spikes during high-intensity military crisis surges.

Our sovereign virtual memory telemetry architecture continuously instruments the PagedAttention memory subsystem across multi-GPU datacenter clusters. Operating at the driver and kernel level, the agent captures physical page allocations, virtual-to-physical address mappings, and page table swap states between GPU HBM and Host DDR5 memory at microsecond resolution.

The telemetry state machine dynamically tunes block size parameters (16 vs 32 tokens per block) and predictive swap-out watermarks based on live incoming tactical query queue depths. When a burst of priority reconnaissance imagery queries enters the cluster, the allocator automatically evicts background batch jobs to host memory while pinning high-priority command sessions in ultra-fast HBM3e pages.

Operating with zero dropped requests across 96-hour continuous crisis simulation exercises, the solution reduces GPU VRAM waste to under 3.5%, achieves a 4.1x boost in concurrent query serving capacity, and maintains deterministic sub-15ms token delivery across all military defense command consoles.

faqs.question: Does PagedAttention telemetry introduce overhead that slows down token generation?
faqs.answer: No. The telemetry hooks are compiled into non-blocking eBPF and CUDA event listeners that consume less than 0.2% of GPU compute capacity.

faqs.question: Can this memory allocation telemetry detect malicious denial-of-service prompt injections?
faqs.answer: Yes. Abnormally ballooning attention allocations are detected instantly and throttled before they exhaust cluster-wide VRAM reserves.

faqs.question: Is this compatible with NVIDIA DGX H100 and customized sovereign ARM64 server architectures?
faqs.answer: Yes. The virtual memory telemetry stack runs natively on x86_64 and ARM64 platforms supporting Linux PREEMPT_RT.
